title: City's 'most haunted' house where a ghostly nun has been spotted
excerpt: The house has been known for many ghostly sightings over the years
content:
A building in Cambridge is widely considered the 'most haunted' in the city following several historic sightings of a ghostly nun. The mysterious figure has allegedly bee seen wandering around Abbey House, which lies on the corner of Beche Road and Abbey Road.

The 17th century house, which is believed to have parts that are older, has often been described as the oldest inhabited house and the most haunted in Cambridge. The house's creepy reputation came to light while a professor from a Cambridge college lived in the house between 1904 and 1910.

During the family's first night staying there, some of them reportedly awoke at midnight to a crashing sound. From 1907 onwards, the house's terrifying nature worsened as the professor reported seeing the ghost of a nun wrapped in a dark robe. The nun did not speak and failed to respond to any questions, but on one occasion, supposedly stood at the foot of the bed while the professor's wife was unwell.

Some local legends say that the house was haunted by the spirit of a nun known as the Grey Lady from a nearby Benedictine nunnery called St Radegund's Priory which was dissolved in 1496.

The nun is said to have often used an underground passage to meet with a secret lover at Barnwell Priory. The priory was the Augustinian priory on which Abbey House was built. So, it may be that the nun is searching for her partner in a place they'd regularly sneak away to.

Other tales include sightings of ghostly animals roaming the house including a red squirrel, which vanished when approached, and a large hare, which sat observing witnesses before disappearing like it was never there. Whereas, another woman claimed she saw a disembodied female head at the foot of her bed.
